about: Every lever this project knows about, what the player actually experiences when you pull it, and how long it takes to show up. Query it with tools/catalog.py. Prose companions: docs/09-alteration-catalog.md and docs/10-novel-alterations.md.

layers.title: Policy and rates
layers.summary: Global dials. No data rows, no patch, no client awareness at all. Applies to the next event that touches it.

layers.title: Content data
layers.summary: Creatures, items, quests, spawns, loot, vendors, events. The client learns about these only by asking the server, so most are patch-free.

layers.title: Mechanics and rules
layers.summary: How existing pieces behave: spell linkage, procs, area auras, conditions, disables, encounter scripts.

layers.title: Systems
layers.summary: New behaviour that spans content: commands, custom protocols, currencies, progression, death rules.

layers.title: Client presentation
layers.summary: Anything the client must know before the server speaks: models, icons, tooltips, spell visuals, map geometry, UI.

layers.title: Novel uses (emergent)
layers.summary: Mechanisms that already exist, used for something they were not built for: the quest log as a HUD, gossip as an app, books as a CMS, the addon channel as a socket.

patch_kinds.title: No client change
patch_kinds.detail: Server sends strings and numbers, or references IDs the client already resolves.

patch_kinds.title: Loose client files
patch_kinds.detail: An addon folder or a patched config: shipped outside the MPQ, no archive rebuild.

patch_kinds.title: DBC rows in an MPQ
patch_kinds.detail: A few hundred bytes of rows added or overridden in an existing table. No art, no new table.

patch_kinds.title: New assets
patch_kinds.detail: Models, textures, maps, sounds, interface files. Out of scope for this project's reuse-first constraint.

entries.title: XP rate
entries.effect: Every kill, quest turn-in and zone discovery pays out multiplied XP; the bar moves visibly faster and alts level in an evening.
verify: kill one mob and watch the XP bar
.modify xp <n> to prove the hook is live
entries.notes: Applies on the next award, no reload needed for subsequent kills. Per-BG rates exist separately.

entries.title: Level cap
entries.effect: Characters keep levelling past 80 up to the cap; every level needs a row in the XP table or the client shows a full bar that never fills.
verify: .character level 79 then kill something
check the XP bar tooltip against player_xp_for_level
entries.notes: Anything above 80 relies on client tables (gt*, scaling stats) that were authored for 80; this is the classic 'raises cap, breaks stats' trap.

entries.title: Starting level, money and loadout
entries.effect: New characters log in already levelled, funded, geared and with spells on the bar; existing characters are untouched.
verify: create a new character and read the combat log / bags
existing alts as a control
entries.notes: Only new characters. Starting items must exist in the client's Item.dbc or they arrive as red ?.

entries.title: Money drops and sinks
entries.effect: Corpses pay more or less; repair, vendor and training costs stay fixed, so the economy gets looser or tighter without touching any item.
verify: in a disposable realm, record coin from the same creature over multiple kills before and after the rate change
compare the sample totals and account for random variation instead of treating one kill as a deterministic assertion
entries.notes: The .modify money command changes a character's wallet; it is a control, not evidence for a drop-rate change. BuyPrice and SellPrice are separate vendor sinks, so isolate those changes from the money-drop rate when measuring the effect.

entries.title: Drop rates by quality
entries.effect: The same loot tables yield noticeably more blues and epics; drop chances move as a whole without editing a single row.
verify: kill the same rare 10 times
compare drop log
entries.notes: Rate.Drop.Item.Referenced controls reference-table rolls specifically; get both wrong and drops look inverted.

entries.title: Reputation pace
entries.effect: Faction bars fill faster; spillover makes one faction's gain nudge its allies, so a single grind unlocks several quartermasters.
verify: on a disposable character, record the same repeatable quest turn-in before and after the rate change
watch the faction bar and check any intended spillover factions separately
entries.notes: Keep the config multiplier, reward-rate rows and spillover template as separate causes in the test; one faction's visible gain does not by itself prove every reputation source or ally spillover is configured.

entries.title: Talent points per level
entries.effect: Each level grants extra talent points, so builds that are impossible at 71 points become reachable.
verify: level a fresh character twice
count points in the talent pane
entries.notes: The client's talent pane draws from its own Talent.dbc/TalentTab.dbc, so you are changing how many points you get, not what is on the tree.

entries.title: Movement speed
entries.effect: Everyone (or every NPC) moves faster; the client renders the motion from server-driven speed changes, so it looks native.
verify: run a straight line and time it
.modify speed 2 for an instant comparison
entries.notes: Above ~3x the client's prediction visibly desyncs; expect rubber-banding, not a patch requirement.

entries.title: Death cost
entries.effect: Corpse runs get longer or shorter, and elite corpses linger; dying feels expensive or cheap without touching combat.
verify: on a test character, measure one PvE corpse-reclaim delay against the configured value
test corpse decay independently; PvP reclaim settings are a separate case
entries.notes: Corpse reclaim delay and corpse decay are distinct behaviors. Use controlled test characters and distinguish PvE from PvP rather than inferring all five settings from one death.

entries.title: Honor, arena points and PvP tokens
entries.effect: PvP currency accrues faster and caps move; PvP tokens make kills drop an existing item as a reward.
verify: win a battleground and check the honor pane
kill a player with PvPToken.Enable = 1 and loot
entries.notes: PvPToken.ItemID must be an item the client already knows; a custom token needs Item.dbc rows.

entries.title: Guild costs
entries.effect: Charters and bank tabs cost what you say; guilds become a real gold sink or a free convenience.
verify: on a disposable test character, compare guild-charter cost with Guild.CharterCost
in a throwaway test guild, check initial bank tabs and a tab purchase without modifying a live guild
verify member-cap behavior only within a controlled test guild
entries.notes: Charter cost, initial tabs, bank-tab purchase prices and member limit are separate settings. Do not validate this by changing an established guild or its bank.

entries.title: Cross-faction play
entries.effect: Both factions share a chat, a group finder and a calendar; the world becomes one population without touching faction data.
verify: log two characters on opposite factions and talk
entries.notes: Purely social unless you also relax faction templates, which changes NPC hostility for everyone.

entries.title: Instance resets and lockouts
entries.effect: Raids reset at your hour; access requirements decide who may enter at all.
verify: inspect the test character's binds with .instance listbinds
verify reset timing using a dedicated test lockout across the configured reset boundary
entries.notes: Do not use an unbind-all command as a routine test; it can clear player lockouts. Access requirements, instance templates and LFG mappings are separate from the scheduled reset setting.

entries.title: Addon channel (server-driven UI)
entries.effect: Turns on the hidden chat channel that carries addon messages, which is how a server can drive a custom UI without a single client file.
verify: .server info or the config value
send a prefixed message from an addon and log it server-side
entries.notes: Off by default on some builds. Without it, a custom panel cannot receive anything from the server.

entries.title: Item attribute enforcement
entries.effect: Decides whether the client's Item.dbc silently overwrites class, subclass, material, inventory type, display and sheath on every item you create.
verify: make an item whose item_template row disagrees with Item.dbc, then look at it in game
entries.notes: The single most confusing knob in item modding: with enforcement on, your SQL stats apply but your SQL appearance does not.

entries.title: A new NPC or mob
entries.effect: A creature with your name, level, faction and model appears where you spawn it; the client is told all of it at query time.
verify: .lookup creature <entry>
.npc add <entry>
hover it: name, level, portrait
entries.notes: The model must be an existing CreatureDisplayInfo id; the name and subname are strings the server sends.

entries.title: Creature difficulty
entries.effect: The same model hits harder, survives longer, resists what you choose; the fight feels different before any new mechanic exists.
verify: fight it at two different modifier values
.damage / .combatstop to reset
entries.notes: Modifiers multiply per-level baselines, so a small change at 80 is a large one at 80 elite.

entries.title: Creature appearance swap
entries.effect: Point a stock creature at a different existing model: instant reskin, no new art, no patch.
verify: .npc set model? or respawn and look
check nothing renders as a naked cube
entries.notes: ~59k creature displays exist; the whole trick is picking one that already animates the way you need.

entries.title: Creature equipment
entries.effect: Weapons and armour appear in the creature's hands and on its body, drawn from item display ids the client already has.
verify: respawn and inspect the model up close
entries.notes: Equipment ids resolve through ItemDisplayInfo, so reusing an existing display id is what keeps this patch-free.

entries.title: Cosmetic auras and mounts on NPCs
entries.effect: Glowing eyes, floating runes, a permanent mount: existing spell visual ids worn as decoration.
verify: respawn and look for the visual
/console check the aura in the unit frame
entries.notes: The client renders auras only for spell ids it knows; an unknown id is silently invisible.

entries.title: Creature dialogue (say, yell, emote)
entries.effect: Custom lines appear in the chat frame in the creature's voice, with your colour coding for say, yell and whisper.
verify: pull it and read the chat frame
.npc say <text> as a live check
entries.notes: Text travels in the chat packet as a string; the client never needs a DBC entry for dialogue.

entries.title: Gossip menus and NPC dialogue trees
entries.effect: A branching conversation with options that can vendor, train, teleport, or hand control to a script.
verify: right-click the NPC and click through options
entries.notes: Option text is a string in the packet; option *behaviour* comes from the option type plus your script.

entries.title: A new quest
entries.effect: Title, objectives, body text, reward and map markers all render normally, as if the quest shipped with the game.
verify: .quest add <id>
read the log entry, then complete and turn in
entries.notes: All quest prose is server-sent, which is why custom quest chains are the highest-value patch-free content.

entries.title: Quest chains and prerequisites
entries.effect: Content unlocks in an order you control: breadcrumbs, attunements, one-time story beats.
verify: on isolated test characters, compare quest acceptance with and without the required predecessor
exercise condition-based gates separately from PrevQuestID links
entries.notes: PrevQuestID and conditions are distinct gating mechanisms; verify the starter relation and the player's quest state as well as the prerequisite row. A static SQL check does not prove the live questgiver path.

entries.title: What a vendor sells
entries.effect: Stock lists change, prices change, and gated items appear only for players who qualify.
verify: open the vendor window
buy with and without the condition met
entries.notes: Money prices need nothing client-side. A token *price* is ItemExtendedCost, which does.

entries.title: Token prices (existing cost id)
entries.effect: The vendor shows 'X tokens' instead of gold, using a cost row the client already has.
verify: open the vendor window: the price line shows items, not coins
entries.notes: Reusing an existing ItemExtendedCost id keeps this patch-free; a new id is a dbc-rows patch.

entries.title: What a trainer teaches
entries.effect: A trainer window that offers exactly the spells you list, at your prices, including spells from other classes.
verify: open the trainer window and learn one
entries.notes: The spell must exist in the client's Spell.dbc or the row is unlearnable.

entries.title: Loot tables
entries.effect: Corpses and chests drop what you decide, with group rolls, guaranteed slots and conditional extras.
verify: kill it and open the loot window
.damage to speed up the loop
entries.notes: Item 0 in a loot row is money. GroupId creates 'one of these' rolls.

entries.title: Shared loot via reference tables
entries.effect: One authored loot list is reused by many creatures, so editing it visibly changes dozens of drop sources at once.
verify: kill two different creatures that share the reference
compare drops
entries.notes: Reference rows roll on their own chance; Rate.Drop.Item.Referenced multiplies them.

entries.title: New item stats on an existing item id
entries.effect: A familiar icon and name with completely different stats, damage, spells and requirements.
verify: .additem <id> and read the tooltip
equip it and check the character sheet
entries.notes: Cheapest item in the game to make. The client shows icon/model from its own Item.dbc, so stats and name are yours.

entries.title: A genuinely new item
entries.effect: A new id with its own icon and model, indistinguishable from a Blizzard item.
verify: after patching and restarting the client: .additem, tooltip, model, no red ?
entries.notes: Item.dbc is 8 int32; the icon lives in ItemDisplayInfo field 3. Both must be in the client's patch, and the server needs matching copies.

entries.title: Item sets and bonuses
entries.effect: Set bonuses fire and the tooltip lists the pieces and their thresholds.
verify: equip two pieces and read the set block in the tooltip
entries.notes: The set block is rendered from the client's ItemSet.dbc, so a set with no client rows is invisible even though the server applies it.

entries.title: Gems, enchants and sockets
entries.effect: A new gem shows the right stats and colour, and sockets accept it.
verify: socket it and read the tooltip delta
entries.notes: Reuse an existing gem's enchant id and you need no patch at all, which is usually enough.

entries.title: Spawn density, packs and patrols
entries.effect: The world feels crowded or empty; packs pull together; rare spawns rotate between points instead of camping one.
verify: .go xyz to the area and count
.npc add for one-offs
entries.notes: Pools are the cheapest way to make a zone feel alive without inventing content.

entries.title: Game objects, doors and chests
entries.effect: Doors that open with a key, chests that loot, braziers that light: existing display ids wearing new behaviour.
verify: .gobject add <entry>
click it and watch the state change
entries.notes: Data0..Data23 change meaning per type; a door's Data0 is a Lock.dbc id, so locks are reused, not invented.

entries.title: Graveyards and spirit healers
entries.effect: Dying in your custom area sends players to the graveyard you picked instead of the nearest stock one.
verify: on a test character, die well inside the mapped zone and record the spirit-healer destination
repeat near the zone boundary to test the actual zone assignment
entries.notes: Check the graveyard_zone mapping against the target core's zone IDs and team rules; the destination observed in a real client/runtime remains an external acceptance check.

entries.title: Area triggers and teleports
entries.effect: Walking into a spot moves the player somewhere else, or fires a script, with the normal loading screen.
verify: walk through the trigger and watch the loading screen
entries.notes: Trigger ids are client-side coordinates, so reuse existing triggers or place triggers on existing geometry.

entries.title: World events and calendars
entries.effect: Content appears and disappears on a schedule; the calendar and world defence messages behave natively.
verify: .event start <id>
.event activelist
entries.notes: The best delivery vehicle for seasonal content because everything else stays untouched.

entries.title: Transports and taxi routes
entries.effect: A boat or zeppelin that actually sails a route players can ride.
verify: board it and watch the crossing
entries.notes: New routes usually need client DBC rows for the path; reuse an existing transport entry when you can.

entries.title: Battleground and arena configuration
entries.effect: Queue sizes, level brackets and rewards change; battleground holidays appear on the calendar.
verify: use the target core's documented test-queue procedure on an isolated realm and check bracket/queue behavior
complete a controlled match and inspect the configured reward delivery
verify holiday/calendar visibility separately from battleground mechanics
entries.notes: Do not rely on the speculative `.bg start?` command. Existing battleground mechanics are server-side; a new PvP UI entry may require client DBC rows, and live queue, reward, and calendar behavior must be tested against the target core/client.

entries.title: Dungeon finder entries and rewards
entries.effect: The dungeon appears in the LFG tool with its reward bag.
verify: open the LFG pane and find it
entries.notes: The LFG list is drawn from the client's LFGDungeons.dbc, so a new listing without rows simply never appears.

entries.title: Mail rewards and letters
entries.effect: Level-up letters, event gifts and compensation mails arrive with items attached.
verify: on a disposable character, trigger only the intended mail source and inspect sender, subject and attachments
log out and back in, then confirm delivery/claim behavior for the selected mail path
entries.notes: Level rewards, loot-driven mail and template-driven message text are separate paths; test the exact one configured. Use a throwaway character and verify item references against local client/server data before claiming the reward is usable.

entries.title: Stat curves and scaling tables
entries.effect: How much agility, crit and dodge a point buys changes, reshaping every class at once.
verify: compare the character sheet before and after
level a test character
entries.notes: The gt* curves are client tables with server overlays; changing only the overlay desyncs the character sheet from combat.

entries.title: Weather
entries.effect: Zones get rain or snow on a schedule, which the client renders from server weather packets.
verify: use `.weather <type> <intensity>` as an immediate GM control and observe the target client
verify the scheduled zone behavior separately; a GM override does not prove game_weather scheduling
entries.notes: The command is an immediate control, not proof that zone scheduling is configured. Confirm that the chosen weather type renders on the exact client build and that the tested zone/schedule matches the row.

entries.title: Vehicles and passengers
entries.effect: Click a vehicle, take a seat, ride: seats and accessories come from existing seat ids.
verify: right-click the vehicle and watch the seat UI
entries.notes: Seat ids come from the client's VehicleSeat.dbc; reuse them rather than inventing rigs.

entries.title: Phasing
entries.effect: The same spot looks different to different players: a burned village for one, an intact one for another.
verify: two characters with different progress, side by side
entries.notes: Phase ids in 3.3.5 are bitmasks on spawns plus condition gating, not a scriptable scene graph.

entries.title: A scripted boss encounter
entries.effect: Phases, adds, timers, a yell on pull, a lockout that records the kill.
verify: .instance stats
kill it and check the encounter credit
entries.notes: Everything the client sees is existing spells, existing emotes and text strings.

entries.title: Spell numbers
entries.effect: Damage, healing, cost, duration and cooldown of an existing spell change for everyone, tooltip and all — because the server sends the numbers it uses.
verify: cast it and read the tooltip next to the combat log
entries.notes: spell_dbc is a server overlay. Tooltips are built from what the server sends, so overlay changes usually show; icon and visual ids still come from the client.

entries.title: Cooldown overrides
entries.effect: A spell's cooldown shortens without editing 234-field rows; the client's sweep animates to the new value.
verify: on an isolated character, record the spell's baseline and changed cooldown using the same rank and conditions
cast again after the cooldown expires and compare the client sweep with actual server usability
entries.notes: Test one known spell without other cooldown modifiers first. The client sweep is presentation evidence; successful recast timing is the server behavior check.

entries.title: Threat modifiers
entries.effect: Tanking abilities generate more or less threat; the fight's shape changes without new tooltips.
verify: on a disposable encounter, repeat the same pull with controlled actions and record which player the creature targets
use a compatible threat meter if available; compare its readings separately from target changes
entries.notes: Threat-meter availability is client/addon dependent, and target selection is only a coarse signal. Keep spell_threat changes distinct from spell_bonus_data damage/healing modifiers.

entries.title: Linked spells (on-cast riders)
entries.effect: Casting one spell also applies another: a charge that leaves a trail, a heal that grants a shield.
verify: cast the trigger and watch the second aura appear
entries.notes: Both spells must be client-known ids. This is the cheapest way to invent a 'new' ability.

entries.title: Proc behaviour
entries.effect: Existing spells start reacting to hits, crits or casts in new ways; the proc flash is the client's own.
verify: use a disposable character and a target known to permit the configured proc event
record enough attempts to separate a low-probability proc from a missing trigger; test the no-proc control too
entries.notes: A single failed roll does not show that the proc is broken, and training dummies may not satisfy every proc condition. Keep hit/crit/cast events and any cooldown or proc-chance limits explicit in the test.

entries.title: Spell scripts
entries.effect: A spell can do things the DBC cannot express: spawn, teleport, set data, or chain to a script.
verify: on the target core build, cast from the documented trigger and check the expected scripted effect
exercise a negative path such as invalid target or unmet condition and confirm no unintended mutation
entries.notes: The SQL binding and C++ ScriptName/hook must both be present for a core script to run. A successful database row load alone does not prove the callback is registered or that client-visible spell data is available.

entries.title: Zone-wide auras
entries.effect: Entering a zone applies a buff or debuff automatically: cold, corruption, a sanctuary rule.
verify: on test characters with matching and non-matching conditions, cross into the configured zone and check the aura
cross back out and re-enter to check removal and reapplication behavior
entries.notes: Zone/area, quest and other spell_area conditions are separate inputs. Test both sides of a boundary and the relevant character state; a single entrance check does not verify cleanup or every condition path.

entries.title: Portals and teleports by spell
entries.effect: A spell that moves the caster or target to coordinates you choose: mage portals, summons, escape hatches.
verify: on an isolated test realm, cast from a known start location and record map, position and orientation after arrival
test each intended map/instance destination and caster-versus-target behavior separately
entries.notes: Use coordinates validated for the target map and safe landing area. A server-side teleport destination does not imply a custom map or new client assets are available.

entries.title: Buff stacking rules
entries.effect: Decide which buffs overwrite each other, so two similar effects coexist instead of cancelling.
verify: apply the two test buffs in order A then B and record aura presence and effect
repeat in reverse order and after relog/reapply to distinguish stacking from replacement rules
entries.notes: Buff-bar icons alone do not prove both effects are active. Use controlled test spells and check both aura state and gameplay effect; ranking and other stack rules may be independent.

entries.title: 10/25 and heroic splits
entries.effect: The same boss can select a difficulty-specific spell version without duplicating the creature entry.
verify: run the same encounter in two difficulty modes supported by the target instance and compare the selected spell behavior
check instance encounter/difficulty state alongside casts; do not infer the variant from raid size alone
entries.notes: The mapping only applies when the target core and instance expose the relevant difficulties and encounter IDs. Client UI visibility and actual server-side spell selection are separate checks.

entries.title: SmartAI behaviour
entries.effect: Summons, casts, emotes and phases on timers or triggers, with no compiled code.
verify: .reload smart_scripts or restart, then pull
entries.notes: AIName must be SmartAI. Events/actions/targets are numeric enums from SmartScriptMgr.h.

entries.title: Patrols and formations
entries.effect: NPCs walk routes and move as a pack, which reads as 'real world' far more than better stats do.
verify: spawn one controlled test creature on an isolated path and confirm movement through each waypoint in order
observe a full route cycle and formation spacing after reload/restart using a unique path ID
entries.notes: Waypoint path assignment, point order and formation membership are separate data links. Avoid reusing live spawn/path IDs during tests; check the target core's supported waypoint table/script path.

entries.title: The conditions engine
entries.effect: Any row anywhere can be gated on quest, item, aura, reputation, level, achievement or skill.
verify: test with a character that meets and one that does not
entries.notes: The single most reusable mechanic in the schema: it is how you gate vendors, loot, gossip and spawns without code.

entries.title: Disabling content
entries.effect: Spells, quests, maps or battlegrounds stop being available, with the client's own 'unavailable' messaging.
verify: try the disabled action and read the error
entries.notes: The clean way to run a 'different expansion' without deleting rows.

entries.title: Respawn and pooling
entries.effect: Rares rotate, camps refill at your pace, and killing one thing releases another.
verify: in a disposable test area, record baseline respawn times for each linked/pool member
kill one member and observe pool release, respawn order and timer over more than one cycle
entries.notes: Pool selection and linked-respawn delays can be randomized or affected by other rows; one kill is not a reliable timing proof. Test only controlled spawns and keep production rare/respawn data untouched.

entries.title: A custom chat command
entries.effect: Players type a command and something happens; the .help list can document it.
verify: as an ordinary player, confirm the command is listed by .help <command>
invoke it with valid, missing and malformed arguments; confirm permission failures do not mutate state
entries.notes: The lightest-weight system hook there is: no client awareness, no UI.

entries.title: Server-to-UI protocol
entries.effect: A custom panel shows live server state: timers, scores, progression, anything you serialise into a message.
verify: replay the vectors in examples/vault-terminal/PROTOCOL.md
make test-engineer (spec, Lua, C++ and model agree)
send a message in game and watch the frame update
entries.notes: This is how you get a real UI without a client patch: ship only an addon folder, keep all truth on the server. Worked example: examples/vault-terminal (protocol, addon, module, SQL).

entries.title: A custom currency and its sink
entries.effect: Players earn a token by playing and spend it at your NPC; the UI is a gossip menu plus an existing item.
verify: on a test character, record token balance before earning, after earning and after spending
test insufficient funds and a repeated/competing spend attempt; verify no unintended extra debit or reward
entries.notes: Free if the token is an existing item. A new token item drags in Item.dbc rows, and an ExtendedCost price drags in ItemExtendedCost rows. If the sink is custom code, define transaction, retry and concurrency semantics rather than relying on the displayed bag count alone.

entries.title: Account-wide progression
entries.effect: Doing something on one character unlocks something for the account: vendors, teleports, a difficulty tier.
verify: unlock on one character, relog, then check a second character on the same account
check a character on a different test account to confirm the unlock scope is not global
entries.notes: Needs storage you own (a character or account table) plus conditions that read it. Verify the chosen account/character key, persistence across restart, and cleanup/reset policy; a second character alone does not prove account isolation.

entries.title: Custom death rules (hardcore, no-release)
entries.effect: Dying means something: a broadcast, a level loss, a permanent flag, a graveyard-only existence.
verify: on a disposable test character, trigger death and confirm the configured rule and announcement
relog and test release/reclaim, resurrection and any permanent flag or penalty for the stated policy
entries.notes: The client shows death exactly as it always does; the meaning is entirely yours. Validate all death/release paths and persistence before enabling a punitive rule; a broadcast alone proves neither enforcement nor recovery behavior.

entries.title: Dynamic difficulty scaling
entries.effect: The same instance is tuned for the group that enters, so a 3-man run and a 5-man run both feel right.
verify: on an isolated instance, record the same creature's health and damage with two controlled group sizes
repeat with a solo/party control and check caps, reset behavior and non-scaled creatures
entries.notes: Scaling policy is custom module behavior, not supplied by HealthModifier alone. Validate the target AllCreatureScript hook and spawn timing on the exact core; a health comparison does not prove balanced damage, healing, bosses or a fair encounter.

entries.title: Custom loot logic
entries.effect: Loot that reacts: pity timers, guaranteed drops after N kills, per-player rolls.
verify: on a disposable realm and fresh test state, run the same kill sequence with a baseline control and record every result
test the guaranteed-drop/pity threshold and per-player case separately; repeat enough trials to expose random variance
entries.notes: A short random sample cannot prove a pity timer or guarantee. If the behavior persists across sessions, its state needs explicit storage, retry, concurrency and reset semantics; ordinary creature_loot_template rows do not implement those policies by themselves.

entries.title: Warden and integrity checks
entries.effect: Clients running altered memory or wrong files get caught; the check results are server-side.
verify: on a disposable test realm, enable the intended check and confirm its result is recorded with the expected account/session context
test a controlled known-good client and an approved test violation; verify alert handling and false-positive recovery without treating Warden as a content or patch validator
entries.notes: Warden validates a narrow set of things; it is not a content validator, and it cannot confirm a player has your patch.

entries.title: Adding or overriding a DBC row
entries.effect: The client can resolve something it could not before: an icon, a tooltip line, a set block, a spell visual.
verify: validate the row against the target build-12340 schema and paired client/server data before install
on a clean test client, restart and exercise the item/spell; inspect tooltip, icon/visual and client logs for missing or mismatched references
entries.notes: Same field count, same field order, or the client refuses the table (and the server logs a field-count mismatch).

entries.title: Shipping a patch archive
entries.effect: Every player who updates sees the new rows simultaneously, and nobody who skips the update does.
verify: on a clean supported client, verify the installed archive name, manifest and checksum before launch
launch with and without the patch in a disposable client profile; confirm expected assets and capture load errors without overwriting stock data
entries.notes: Numeric patches outrank the stock patch-3; locale files outrank root files in most locales but not all. Manifest + checksum is how you know.

entries.title: A custom UI frame
entries.effect: A panel that does not exist in the stock UI: scoreboards, trackers, a custom bank, a talent planner.
verify: on a clean build-12340 client, confirm the addon loads without Lua errors and the frame anchors at expected UI scales
test show/hide, /reload, relog and disable/uninstall cleanup; confirm saved variables are scoped and no stock UI state is left altered
entries.notes: Addons are client files but not MPQ entries: ship them as a folder and no patch archive is involved. 3.3.5 uses global API functions (no C_ namespaces).

entries.title: Live data in a custom frame
entries.effect: The frame shows numbers that come from the server in real time, not values baked into the addon.
verify: change the server-side value and confirm the frame updates without /reload
test malformed, oversized, out-of-order and unauthorized messages; verify bounds, rate limits and no client-authoritative state changes
entries.notes: 255-char message cap and rate limits; batch and compress if you need more.

entries.title: Tooltip augmentation
entries.effect: Extra lines on any tooltip: drop locations, set progress, your own currency price.
verify: on an uncached test item and a cached item, verify the tooltip eventually shows exactly one correct augmentation
test nil/unavailable item data, repeated tooltip opens and addon disable; check for Lua errors or duplicate lines
entries.notes: GetItemInfo returns nil until the client has the item, so hook the update path rather than the first draw.

entries.title: Nameplates, minimap and world overlays
entries.effect: Markers, markers on the map, custom nameplate text: direction and discovery aids that feel native.
verify: on a clean build-12340 test client, verify map markers on WorldMapFrame and minimap overlays separately
enable a controlled test nameplate and verify the addon hook, text and cleanup when the unit leaves view
entries.notes: World map, minimap and nameplate hooks are distinct addon surfaces; passing one says nothing about the others. Test only against the target 3.3.5a API/interface and confirm the addon is enabled—retail UI APIs are not interchangeable.

entries.title: Reusing existing sounds
entries.effect: A roar, a bell, a coin: any of the client's existing SoundEntries ids can be played on an event.
verify: on the target client, trigger the event and confirm the intended existing SoundEntries ID plays at expected volume
test a missing/invalid ID and repeated triggers; check client logs and ensure no new-file asset is assumed without a patch
entries.notes: New audio files need an asset patch; existing ids need nothing.

entries.title: Reusing existing models and textures
entries.effect: New content that looks authored, because it is: Blizzard's art, your arrangement.
verify: in a clean target client, compare the reused display/model/texture with its source and check all intended equipment/animation states
inspect the client log and all referenced client/server display IDs; verify the result survives relog and works for another viewer
entries.notes: The whole point of the reuse-first constraint: recolor-by-composition instead of importing art.

entries.title: New models and textures
entries.effect: Art that never shipped with the game.
verify: run asset-format and reference checks for the target client build before packaging, including model, texture and display linkage
on a clean client with the patch installed, inspect representative animations/attachments and logs; test a client without the patch to confirm failure is detected
entries.notes: Out of scope here: it is an art pipeline (conversion, attachment points, LOD, animation names) and every mistake looks like a client crash.

entries.title: New maps and terrain
entries.effect: A place that is not in the game: new geometry, new minimap, new zone name.
verify: validate map/area IDs, ADT/WDT references and client/server coordinates against the target build before packaging
on a clean patched client and isolated server, enter and exit safely; inspect minimap/world-map/area data, terrain seams and logs
entries.notes: The most expensive alteration in this catalog. Reusing an existing instanced map's unused geometry is the budget alternative.

entries.title: Interface and loading screens
entries.effect: A realm that looks like its own game before the first character loads.
verify: on a clean target client, exercise login, realm selection, character selection and loading screens with the skin installed
test missing/corrupt asset fallback and a stock-client control; preserve a recovery path before distributing changes that affect login
entries.notes: Cosmetic and high-risk: wrong text or layout breaks the login flow for everyone.

entries.title: New achievements
entries.effect: A new entry in the achievements pane with its own criteria and reward.
verify: open the achievements pane and find it
earn it on a test character
entries.notes: The pane is entirely client DBC driven; the server overlay alone shows nothing.

entries.title: New talents and talent trees
entries.effect: New nodes on the tree with working icons and tooltips.
verify: on paired clean test client/server data, verify each talent/tab row, prerequisites, icons and tooltip IDs in the talent pane
spend and refund points at boundaries with rate/respec controls; relog and confirm server state, point totals and invalid-node handling
entries.notes: Raising Rate.Talent gives more points; new *nodes* need client rows and are notoriously fragile.

entries.title: New titles
entries.effect: A selectable title in the character pane.
verify: on the target client, confirm the new CharTitles.dbc ID appears in the title selector after a clean restart/cache check
test title unlock/award separately and compare the client row with the server chartitles_dbc data
entries.notes: A client DBC row makes the title selectable/displayable; it does not grant or unlock the title. Keep the client row, server overlay and award path in sync, and verify the entry from local build-12340 data before release.

entries.title: New currency in the currency tab
entries.effect: A tracked currency with an icon in the player's currency pane.
verify: on paired target client/server data, confirm the currency row, icon and intended balance display in the currency pane
earn and spend through the intended server path, then relog and check balance persistence plus missing/invalid currency-ID behavior
entries.notes: Without a client row, a custom currency still exists server-side — it just has no place to display itself.

entries.title: In-game books and printed pages
entries.effect: Right-clicking the item opens a real book window with pages you wrote, chained by NextPageID.
verify: give yourself the item and right-click it
walk the page chain to the last page
entries.notes: page_text is (ID, Text, NextPageID); the reader UI is stock. Any readable book item can be repurposed, so long-form lore, newspapers and manuals cost no client files.

entries.title: Readable signs and plaques
entries.effect: Click a banner, sign or gravestone and a page opens with your text.
verify: .gobject add <entry> and click it
entries.notes: GameObject type 9 (TEXT) reads Data0 as a page_text id; Data1 is language, Data2 page material. Display comes from an existing GameObjectDisplayInfo id.

entries.title: The gossip window as an application
entries.effect: A multi-screen application: menus that branch, options that only appear when conditions pass, prompt boxes for input.
verify: click through three levels of menus
verify a gated option is hidden for an unqualified character
entries.notes: ActionMenuID makes an option open another menu, so the graph is a UI, not a single screen. Cost: text, conditions, one NPC.

entries.title: Player-entered codes (a keypad, a PIN)
entries.effect: The client asks the player to type a code into a box; the matching one unlocks the option.
verify: try a wrong code, then the right one
entries.notes: BoxCoded is the required code and BoxText is the prompt; money-box input (BoxMoney) accepts an amount instead. Both are stock UI — no addon, no patch. Good for vaults, tickets, and 'enter your voucher code' events.

entries.title: The quest log as a persistent HUD
entries.effect: A panel in the top-right of every player's screen that shows objectives and counters, updating as they act — a scoreboard nobody had to install.
verify: accept the quest and watch the objective counter move
reload the UI: it persists
entries.notes: Up to 25 quests are tracked natively, each with numbered objectives and map markers. Season scores, kill counters, collection progress and 'daily checklist' designs fit here; the client renders it all as quests.

entries.title: Custom map markers
entries.effect: Pins on the world map pointing at places you invented, with tooltips, without a single addon.
verify: open the map while the quest is active
check the marker sits where your content is
entries.notes: quest_poi rows are per quest; points_of_interest gives standing markers. This is the cheapest way to make a custom area discoverable.

entries.title: A request/response socket between UI and server
entries.effect: The addon asks a question with arguments; the server answers with state. A real protocol in a 255-byte frame.
verify: make test-master (fuzz, midnight, reconnect)
kill the server and confirm the UI degrades gracefully
entries.notes: This is the difference between a static panel and a live one: client-side polling, server-side push, and commands bound to keys or macros. Batch small messages; rate limits and the 255-char cap are the design constraints. Worked example: examples/vault-terminal (protocol, addon, module, SQL).

entries.title: Client-side telemetry
entries.effect: The client reports what it can see — zone, spec, group composition, addon version — and the server records it.
verify: watch the server log while a player moves and respecs
entries.notes: Useful for tuning difficulty per real group, detecting players without your addon, and knowing which of your content hooks are actually being used. No prefix registration exists in 3.3.5a; the server claims the prefix in its own hook (see examples/vault-terminal).

entries.title: Two places at the same coordinates
entries.effect: The same spot is a ruin for one player and a village for another, or a clean arena for a spectator.
verify: walk two characters with different progress to the same point
entries.notes: Phasing is a bitmask on spawns plus conditions, not a scene graph: you cannot move terrain, but you can swap every creature and object, which is most of the effect.

entries.title: Triggered camera sequences
entries.effect: Clicking an object plays one of the client's existing cinematic camera sequences: a real cutscene on demand.
verify: .gobject add <camera entry> and click it
confirm the camera plays and control returns
entries.notes: GameObject type 13 (CAMERA) reads Data1 as a CinematicSequences id. The sequences themselves are client assets, so reusing an existing id is what keeps this patch-free.

entries.title: Environmental damage without spells
entries.effect: Standing in the wrong place hurts: a radius, a damage range and a school, configured on the object itself.
verify: .gobject add <areadamage entry> and stand in it
entries.notes: GameObject type 12 (AREADAMAGE) has radius, damageMin/Max and damageSchool. Cheaper than a spell and impossible to dispel.

entries.title: Proximity devices
entries.effect: Something fires when a player comes near: a spell, a trap, a bomb on spawn, silently or stealthed.
verify: .gobject add <trap entry> and walk in
entries.notes: GameObject type 6 (TRAP) has spellId, type (persistent / despawns / bomb on spawn), cooldown, startDelay, stealthed and invisible flags. This is how you write 'the floor is dangerous' without a boss.

entries.title: A gate that needs several players
entries.effect: Opening it requires N people standing together, which turns a doorway into a social mechanic.
verify: try alone (nothing), then with the required number
entries.notes: GameObject type 18 (SUMMONING_RITUAL) takes reqParticipants plus the spell that completes it — the stock UI draws the ritual circle for you.

entries.title: Objects that spawn defenders
entries.effect: A banner or totem that spawns creatures until its charges run out: reinforcements, turrets, wave defence.
verify: .gobject add <guardpost entry> and watch the spawns
entries.notes: GameObject type 21 (GUARDPOST) stores a creatureID and charges. Combined with traps and SmartAI this is a tower-defence event built from four tables.

entries.title: Objects that cast on the player
entries.effect: Click a device and it casts a spell on you: a buff station, a vending machine, a teleporter pad.
verify: .gobject add <spellcaster entry> and click it
entries.notes: GameObject type 22 (SPELLCASTER): Data0 spellId, Data1 charges, Data2 partyOnly, Data3 allowMounted. The spell must be client-known — reuse an existing one and nothing needs patching.

entries.title: Boolean logic without code
entries.effect: AND, OR and NOT over quests, items, auras, reputation, level, achievement and skill — a predicate language the schema already speaks.
verify: build (quest A AND NOT item B) OR reputation ≥ X and test four characters
entries.notes: Rows in the same ElseGroup are OR; different groups are AND; NegativeCondition inverts. Once you see it as logic, gating stops being code.

entries.title: Progressive unlock and kill switches
entries.effect: Content exists but is switched off until a date, an event, or your decision: seasonal rollout, staged launches, emergency off-switches.
verify: disable a spell and confirm the client's own refusal message
.event start <id> to enable a block
entries.notes: disables handles spells, quests, maps and battlegrounds; game_event handles scheduling. Together they are a feature-flag system with no code.

entries.title: SmartAI as the world's event loop
entries.effect: Timers, spawns, emotes, casts and phases on any creature or object: a general scripting layer that needs no compilation.
verify: .reload smart_scripts (or restart), then watch a full cycle
entries.notes: The numeric enums are the API (SmartScriptMgr.h). Most 'we need a module for this' ideas are four rows of smart_scripts.

entries.title: Quests as an explicit state machine
entries.effect: States are quests, transitions are prerequisites: a story, a tutorial, or a progression tree that the players can see in their log.
verify: walk the chain in and out of order
entries.notes: Because quest state is per character and permanent, this is the cheapest persistent per-player state the schema offers.

entries.title: Mail as an asynchronous queue
entries.effect: Deliveries that arrive while the player is offline: compensation, daily gifts, story episodes, auction-style payouts.
verify: log out, trigger the mail, log in and open the mailbox
entries.notes: Mail is the only delivery channel that survives absence, and it accepts items, money and text.

entries.title: Items as game pieces
entries.effect: A deck, a hand, a collection: items and enchant rolls are discrete pieces players can hold, trade and wager.
verify: build a small deck and trade a card
entries.notes: The trade window, mail and the auction house are the protocols; item IDs are the pieces. Random-suffix rolls (item_enchantment_template) give variance without new items.

entries.title: Custom text in every client locale
entries.effect: Your dialogue, quest text, gossip and server messages appear in the player's own language.
verify: switch the client locale and re-read the same content
entries.notes: Locale tables exist for most content; acore_string/module_string cover server-generated messages. Text is server-side, so this costs no client files.

entries.title: Class-less or free-form characters
entries.effect: Characters start with an unusual kit — every class's basics, or none — and progression comes from content instead of the class frame.
verify: create a character and inspect the spellbook
verify the action bar is populated
entries.notes: The client's class UI stays as it is; you are changing what the character knows, not what the game thinks a class is. Some UI expectations (talents, trainers) will not match.

entries.title: Instances as persistent state
entries.effect: A run remembers what happened: encounter credit, lockouts, and access that changes as the run progresses.
verify: .instance stats before and after a kill
entries.notes: This is how a custom dungeon becomes a campaign rather than a room full of mobs.

entries.title: A shop that changes per player
entries.effect: The same merchant offers different stock to a fresh character, a veteran, and someone mid-event.
verify: open the vendor with three characters at different stages
entries.notes: Conditions on vendor rows are evaluated per player, so one NPC can be a whole shop tier system.
